You will compare one known error in a data agent's work against a ranked list of items produced by a reviewer. Your job is to decide whether any item in the list identifies this known error, and if so, which one.

An item identifies the known error only if both of these hold:
- It is about the same thing: the same table, and the same column, computation, filter, or join.
- It points to the same problem: what the item says is wrong, assumed, or missing is the same as what went wrong in the known error. It does not matter whether the item is phrased as an assumption the agent made ("the agent assumes ...") or as a problem in the work ("this does not match ..."); judge by meaning.

An item does not count if it only says that something may be wrong without saying what, such as "this column may be computed incorrectly". An item about the same column but a different problem does not count.

If more than one item identifies the error, report the highest-ranked one. If you are unsure, say so rather than guessing.

Return a JSON object with:
- "verdict": "match", "no_match", or "unsure".
- "rank": the position of the matching item (1 is the top), or null.
- "quote": the exact words from the matching item that show it identifies the error, or null.
- "reason": one short sentence.

=== Known error ===
Table: stg_pendo__poll_event
What the agent's work assumed: url 去掉首尾空格就行
What was actually required or true: 不以 http:// 或 https:// 开头的置空

=== Reviewer's ranked list for this table ===
[
  {
    "rank": 1,
    "item": {
      "problem": "Rows with NULL required identifiers, failed numeric ID casts, or invalid occurrence timestamps are retained.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "evidence_in_work": "TRY_CAST(account_id AS BIGINT), TRY_CAST(app_id AS BIGINT); no poll_event filters",
      "source": "account_id, guide_id, poll_id, occurred_at, visitor_id, app_id: constraints: [not_null]",
      "reason": "Invalid responses can participate in latest-NPS selection or lose their account association."
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 2,
    "item": {
      "problem": "Non-HTTP(S) URLs are retained after whitespace cleanup.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "evidence_in_work": "CASE WHEN url IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE NULLIF(TRIM(...), '') END",
      "source": "url IS NULL OR url ~ '^https?://'; on_failure: nullify_field",
      "reason": "The required optional-field validation is missing."
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 3,
    "item": {
      "problem": "Server names and user agents are normalized without a specified correction rule.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "evidence_in_work": "elif n in ('server_name','user_agent','url')",
      "source": "server_name: data_type: VARCHAR(255); user_agent: data_type: VARCHAR(255)",
      "reason": "This can replace meaningful source formatting or empty values."
    }
  },
  {
    "rank": 4,
    "item": {
      "problem": "IPv4 validation accepts a different set of strings from the contract expression.",
      "about": "requirement",
      "evidence_in_work": "'^([0-9]{1,3}\\\\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$'",
      "source": "remote_ip ~ '^([0-9]{1,3}){3}[0-9]{1,3}$'",
      "reason": "Optional IP values will differ, even if the implementation's pattern is more conventional."
    }
  }
]
